en: Scientists use PAGASA reports to compare their local weather records with official data from weather stations across the Philippines.
Before drawing a free-body diagram, choose a scale so that the largest force arrow fits on the paper, then use that same scale for every arrow.
The results section includes both the data table and the graph, so the reader can see the numbers and the pattern.
Label every container with the name of its contents and the date before storing it so nobody mistakes one substance for another.
When filtering, place the filter paper as a cone inside the funnel, wet it slightly, and pour the liquid down a glass rod to avoid splashing.
Hold a reagent bottle with the label facing your palm and pour slowly so drips do not smear or wash off the label.
PHIVOLCS uses old church records and newspaper reports of past earthquakes to estimate how often a fault moves.
For repeated trials, give each trial its own row in the data table, and label each column with the measurement and its unit.
A class can use the FaultFinder's print button to save a map that shows the school and the nearest fault, which they can attach to a report.
Sunlight gives us both light and heat, and it is the main source of energy for life on Earth.
Scientists repeat each lever measurement three times and use the average force, so a single mistake does not change the answer.
A disaster plan is not just a paper; it is a habit you build by walking the evacuation route and checking your go-bag every few months.
After an earthquake, look for fallen power lines and tell an adult so they can report the danger.
Keep a small copy of your family disaster plan inside your school bag, so you can remember what to do even if you are away from home.
When collecting rocks, wrap each sample in paper, label it with the date and place, and keep the label with the rock.
Coins, paper clips, aluminum foil, metal spoons, and keys are everyday conductors that can complete a simple circuit and light a bulb.
A complete circuit needs four parts: a source like a battery, wires to carry current, a load like a bulb, and a closed path.
A rock identification key works like a branching set of questions, each answer sending you to the next question until the rock is named.
When a species goes extinct, the ecosystem services it provided—like pollination or pest control—are lost, and people lose food and medicine sources.
Earthquakes in the Philippines come from two main sources: fault movements like the Philippine Fault, and subduction at trenches like the Manila Trench.
A model is not an exact copy; it leaves out extra details so scientists can focus on the important parts.
Scientists label the electron shells K, L, M, and N, starting with K as the shell closest to the nucleus.
Even a gentle push can move a light object like a paper boat on water in the direction of the push.
Plot the number of coils on the x-axis and paper clips picked up on the y-axis to see the trend.
Use the same size and type of paper clips for every trial so the test is fair and results are comparable.
Swapping the battery connections flips the electromagnet's poles, but it still attracts the same number of paper clips.
When you disconnect one wire from the battery, the nail drops all paper clips right away because the current stops.
